definition_zh: 庄严的；隆重的；严肃的；郑重其事的
definition_en: formal and serious in a religious or public setting, not cheerful, or made as a serious promise
core_image: 安静的礼堂里人们肃立不语
scene: 婚礼是庄严的场合。The wedding was a solemn occasion.
sceneCN: 这里 solemn 是「庄严的；隆重的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：婚礼是庄严的场合。

senses.title: Formal and grand
senses.definition: formal and serious in a public or religious ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在公共或宗教仪式中正式而严肃的

senses.exampleCN: 婚礼是一个庄严的场合。
senses.why: This is the ceremonial sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是仪式性的义项。

senses.title: Serious in manner

senses.why: A promise borrows the weight of ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 承诺借用了仪式的分量。

intro.en: Solemn comes from Latin sollemnis, meaning fixed or ceremonial.

items.en: Solemne kept the sense of religious formality.

definition_zh: 团结；群体成员因共同处境或共同目标而相互支持、彼此承担
definition_en: the unity and mutual support of people who share a common situation or aim
core_image: 码头工人排成一列，把手里的工具传给下一个人，谁也没有多拿，队伍却一直不断
scene: 洪水退去后，邻村的人带着抽水机和干粮赶来，不问谁家先被淹。Solidarity across the valley brought pumps and food before any official order arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 solidarity 指群体成员因共同处境而相互支持的团结（第 1 个义项：共享目标下的联合）；句意为跨谷的团结在任何官方命令到达之前就送来了抽水机与食物。

pos.zh: 团结；相互支持（不可数，指关系或精神状态）
不同类型的团结（用复数 solidarities，见于社会学讨论）

derivatives.zh: 坚固的；实心的；固体（由拉丁 solidus「坚实、完整」直接借入）
坚固性；可靠性（由 solid 加表示「性质」的后缀构成，从物理坚实转指关系可靠）
使凝固；使巩固（由 solid 加表示「使成为」的后缀构成，转指由松散变为坚实）
巩固；合并（由表示「完全」的拉丁前缀加 solidus 构成，转指把分散之物压成一体）
士兵（由拉丁 solidus「金币」衍生晚期拉丁「领饷者」，从军饷转指拿饷打仗的人）
焊接；焊料（由拉丁 solidare「使坚实」经古法语进入英语，转指用金属把接缝变实）

senses.title: Unity around shared aims
senses.definition: the state in which people with a common aim support one another and accept shared responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 有共同目标的人彼此支持、共同承担的状态
senses.example: Solidarity across the valley brought pumps and food before any official order arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 跨谷的团结在任何官方命令到达之前就送来了抽水机与食物。
senses.why: The word names a bond created by a shared condition, not by a contract: people stand together because they are in the same situation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名由共同处境而非契约造出的纽带：人们站在一起，因为处境相同。

senses.title: Mutual support among workers
senses.definition: the organised mutual support of workers, especially through unions and strikes
senses.definitionCN: 劳动者有组织的相互支持，尤指通过工会与罢工
senses.example: The strike held because solidarity kept other depots from moving the goods.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工得以维持，是因为团结让其他仓库不肯运货。
senses.why: Labour movements gave the word its strongest modern use: support that costs the supporter something.
senses.whyCN: 工人运动给这个词最强的现代用法：支持者自己要付出代价的那种支持。

senses.title: Solidarity as a moral duty
senses.definition: a moral obligation to stand with others who suffer, even when one gains nothing
senses.definitionCN: 与他人共处困境、即使自己无所得也应当站在一起的道德义务
senses.example: She joined the vigil out of solidarity rather than curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 她参加守夜是出于团结，而非好奇。
senses.why: Here the bond becomes a duty: the question is not whether one benefits, but whether one owes support.
senses.whyCN: 这里纽带变成责任：问题不是自己是否受益，而是自己是否应当支持。

senses.title: International solidarity
senses.definition: support across borders for people facing disaster, repression or war
senses.definitionCN: 跨越国界、对遭受灾难、压制或战争的人的支持
senses.example: Aid arrived under the banner of international solidarity.
senses.exampleCN: 援助打着国际团结的旗号到达。
senses.why: The word crosses borders when suffering is treated as a common human condition rather than a national matter.
senses.whyCN: 当苦难被视为共同的人类处境而非一国之事，这个词就跨过国界。

senses.title: Community cohesion
senses.definition: the everyday ties that hold a neighbourhood or village together
senses.definitionCN: 把邻里或村庄拢在一起的日常纽带
senses.example: The annual feast is the village's main expression of solidarity.
senses.exampleCN: 一年一度的宴席是村里团结的主要表达。
senses.why: Community studies use the word for the quiet, repeated acts that make a place hold together.
senses.whyCN: 社区研究用这个词指让一个地方维持不散的安静而重复的行动。

senses.title: The social-insurance solidarity principle
senses.titleCN: 社会保险中的互助原则
senses.definition: the principle that contributors pool risk so that those in need are supported by all
senses.definitionCN: 缴费者共担风险、使有需要者由全体支持的原则
senses.example: Health insurance rests on solidarity, not on individual savings alone.
senses.exampleCN: 医疗保险依靠互助，而不只是个人储蓄。
senses.why: Welfare systems borrowed the word for pooled risk: the healthy support the sick, the young support the old.
senses.whyCN: 福利制度借用这个词表示风险共担：健康者支持病者，年轻者支持年长者。

senses.title: Solidarity with a cause
senses.definition: public support for a group or cause one does not belong to
senses.definitionCN: 对并非自己所属的群体或事业给予的公开支持
senses.example: Writers signed the letter in solidarity with the imprisoned journalists.
senses.exampleCN: 作家们签署这封信，声援被囚的记者。
senses.why: The word can reach outward: one need not share the condition in order to stand with those who endure it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以向外延伸：不必共享处境，也可以站在承受者一边。

senses.title: Abstract: a bond from shared condition
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：共同处境造就的纽带
senses.definition: any bond that arises because people share a condition, risk or fate
senses.definitionCN: 因人们共享处境、风险或命运而产生的任何纽带
senses.example: Solidarity can appear among strangers waiting in the same flooded street.
senses.exampleCN: 团结可以出现在同一条被淹街道上等候的陌生人之间。
senses.why: At its widest the word names the invisible thread that a shared condition spins between people.
senses.whyCN: 推到最宽处，这个词命名共同处境在人与人之间纺出的那根看不见的线。

intro.en: Solidarity comes from French solidarité, built on solidaire 'interdependent', from Latin solidus 'solid, whole'. The political sense is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solidarity 来自法语 solidarité，其基底 solidaire 意为「相互依存的」，再追溯到拉丁 solidus「坚实、完整」。政治义是十九世纪的产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solidus meant 'firm, whole, entire'. It also named a Roman gold coin, which is why soldier and solder belong to the same family.
items.cn: solidus 意为「坚实、完整、整个」。它也是一种罗马金币的名称，因此 soldier 与 solder 同属这一词族。

items.en: The root behind solidus is usually reconstructed as a Indo-European form meaning 'whole'. This is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: solidus 背后的词根通常被重构为一个意为「完整」的印欧形式。这是重构形式，并非有文献记录的词。

items.en: French solidaire meant 'jointly responsible, interdependent', describing people whose obligations are linked.
items.cn: 法语 solidaire 意为「连带负责的、相互依存的」，描述义务彼此相连的人。

items.en: Solidarité named the state of being jointly responsible; it is generally dated to the nineteenth century.
items.cn: solidarité 命名「连带负责」的状态；一般认为它出现在十九世纪。

items.en: English solidarity entered through political and labour writing, where it named support that binds workers or nations.
items.cn: 英语 solidarity 经政治与工人运动写作进入，命名把劳动者或国家绑在一起的支援。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact first French and English uses are not recorded, and the pre-Latin root of solidus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：法语与英语的最早用例没有记录；solidus 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one keeps the 'firm, whole' family together with a coin-derived relative; group two holds words for unity and support.
note.cn: 第一组把「坚实、完整」词族的词与一个由金币义衍生的亲属词放在一起；第二组是联合与支持的同义词。

entries.definition: Firm and whole in a physical sense; solidarity applies that firmness to relations between people.
entries.definitionCN: 物理意义上的坚实与完整；solidarity 把这种坚实用于人与人的关系。

entries.definition: The quality of being physically solid or reliable; it names a property, not a social bond.
entries.definitionCN: 物理上坚实或可靠的属性；它命名属性，不命名社会纽带。

entries.definition: To press separate things into one firm body; solidarity is the resulting social bond, not the act of pressing.
entries.definitionCN: 把分散之物压成一个坚实的整体；solidarity 是形成的社会纽带，而非压的动作。

entries.definition: From Late Latin solidarius 'one serving for pay', from solidus as a coin. It is a relative by way of money, not of unity.
entries.definitionCN: 来自晚期拉丁 solidarius「领饷服役者」，其 solidus 指金币。它经由钱而非经由团结与这个词同族。

entries.definition: The state of being one whole; solidarity adds mutual support and shared responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 成为一个整体的状态；solidarity 还加上相互支持与共同责任。

entries.definition: The force that keeps a group together; it can be measured, while solidarity is also a moral stance.
entries.definitionCN: 把群体拢在一起的力量；它可被测量，而 solidarity 也是一种道德立场。

entries.definition: Warm friendship among people who share an activity; it is lighter and more personal than solidarity.
entries.definitionCN: 共享活动者之间温暖的友情；它比 solidarity 更轻、更私人。

entries.definition: People helping one another in practice, often through organised networks; solidarity is the bond that motivates such aid.
entries.definitionCN: 人们在实践中互相帮助，常通过有组织的网络；solidarity 是推动这种援助的纽带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Solidus meant whole and firm, so solidarity is a group holding together as one body.
normal.cn: solidus 意为完整而坚实，所以 solidarity 是一个群体作为一个整体抱在一起。

normal.en: French solidaire means jointly responsible, which is why the word is about obligations, not only feelings.
normal.cn: 法语 solidaire 意为连带负责，所以这个词关乎义务，不只是感情。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the direction: in solidarity with, show solidarity, international solidarity.
normal.cn: 固定说法显示方向：声援、表示团结、国际团结。

normal.en: The same root gives consolidate, which makes separate things firm as one.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 consolidate，把分散之物压成坚实的一体。

normal.en: Soldier belongs by way of the gold coin solidus, a relative through money rather than unity.
normal.cn: soldier 经由金币 solidus 同族，是同过钱而非同过团结的亲属。

abstract.en: Picture dock workers passing tools down a line, nobody taking more than needed.
abstract.cn: 想象码头工人把工具沿队伍传下去，谁也没有多拿。

abstract.en: Picture strangers in a flooded street forming a chain without being asked.
abstract.cn: 想象被淹街道上的陌生人不用谁招呼就拉成一条链。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose every plank carries part of the weight of the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，每块板都承担下一块的一部分重量。

examples.en: Neighbours brought generators in solidarity after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，邻居们出于团结送来发电机。

examples.en: The union called for solidarity with the locked-out workers.
examples.cn: 工会呼吁声援被拒之门外的工人。

examples.en: Health systems rely on solidarity between the healthy and the ill.
examples.cn: 医疗体系依靠健康者与病者之间的互助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「索里 达 瑞提」——大家抱成一个完整坚实的整体 → 团结

root: 法语 solidarité「连带责任」← solidaire「相互依存的」← 拉丁 solidus「坚实、完整」；solidus 更深词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with unity around a shared aim, then move to workers, moral duty, international support, community ties, pooled risk, support for a cause and finally any bond made by a shared condition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从围绕共同目标的联合出发，经过劳动者、道德责任、国际支援、社区纽带、风险共担、对事业的声援，最后是任何由共同处境造就的纽带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people passing a heavy tool hand to hand, no one keeping it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列人把沉重的工具一手传一手，谁都不把它留下。

branches.en: THE BOND AND THE VILLAGE: unity around an aim, and the quiet daily ties that hold a place together.
branches.cn: 纽带与村庄：围绕目标的联合，以及把地方拢住的安静日常纽带。

branches.en: ORGANISED SUPPORT: workers acting through unions, and contributors pooling risk in insurance.
branches.cn: 有组织的支持：劳动者通过工会行动，缴费者在保险中风险共担。

branches.en: DUTY AND CAUSE: support owed to those who suffer, and support offered to those one does not belong to.
branches.cn: 责任与事业：对受苦者应尽的支援，以及对非所属群体的公开声援。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: suffering treated as a common human condition.
branches.cn: 跨越国界：苦难被视为共同的人类处境。

branches.en: THE THREAD: the widest reading names the invisible bond that a shared condition spins.
branches.cn: 那根线：最宽的读法命名共同处境纺出的看不见的纽带。

sceneCN: 这里 solubility 指某物质在特定溶剂中能被溶解的能力与数量（第 1 个义项：溶解的能力）；句意为糖的溶解度随温度稳定上升。图中可辨识物件：烧杯、温度计、记录本、糖。

senses.title: The ability of a substance to dissolve
senses.definition: the capacity of a solid or gas to enter a liquid and become part of it
senses.definitionCN: 固体或气体进入液体并成为其中一部分的能力
senses.example: The solubility of sugar rises sharply with temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 糖的可溶性随温度急剧上升。
senses.why: the noun adds -ity 'state or quality' to soluble, so it names the quality rather than the substance that has it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在 soluble 后加 -ity「状态、性质」，命名的是性质，而不是拥有性质的物质。

senses.title: The measured amount that dissolves
senses.titleCN: 可测定的溶解数量（溶解度）
senses.definition: the quantity of a substance that a fixed amount of solvent can take at a given temperature
senses.definitionCN: 在一定温度下，固定量溶剂所能容纳的物质量
senses.example: The solubility of table salt is about thirty-six grams per hundred grams of water.
senses.exampleCN: 食盐的溶解度约为每一百克水三十六克。
senses.why: once chemists weigh the substance and the solvent, the quality becomes a number, and the same noun covers both.
senses.whyCN: 化学家一旦称量溶质与溶剂，性质就变成数字，同一个名词覆盖两者。

senses.title: A relation to a named solvent
senses.definition: the degree to which a substance dissolves in the particular liquid named
senses.definitionCN: 某物质在被点名的液体中溶解的程度
senses.example: Its solubility in alcohol makes it useful for tinctures.
senses.exampleCN: 它在酒精中的溶解性使它适用于酊剂。
senses.why: a capacity is always a capacity in something, so the noun regularly takes the name of the solvent.
senses.whyCN: 能力总是对某物而言的能力，因此这个名词常带溶剂名。

senses.title: The property studied in pharmacy
senses.titleCN: 药物学关注的溶解性质
senses.definition: the extent to which a drug dissolves in body fluids, which governs how quickly it reaches the blood
senses.definitionCN: 药物在体液中溶解的程度，决定它多快进入血液
senses.example: The drug's low solubility limits how much reaches the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药溶解度低，限制了进入血液的药量。
senses.why: pharmacy applies the chemical measure to a tablet in the body, so the quality becomes a predictor of effect.
senses.whyCN: 药物学把化学量度用到了体内的药片上，于是这一性质成了药效的预测指标。

senses.title: The quality of a problem being solvable
senses.titleCN: 问题可以被解决的程度
senses.definition: the degree to which a difficulty or dispute admits a workable answer
senses.definitionCN: 困难或争端能获得可行答案的程度
senses.example: The solubility of the dispute depended on a neutral chair.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端能否化解，取决于一位中立的会议主持。
senses.why: the figurative sense transfers the chemical measure to problems: some loosen easily and some hardly at all.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义把化学量度搬到问题上：有些容易松开，有些几乎松不开。

senses.title: How far a plan can be made to work
senses.titleCN: 方案可以被化解、被推动的程度
senses.definition: the extent to which a plan, difficulty or objection can be worked through rather than left standing
senses.definitionCN: 某个方案、困难或反对意见能被处理掉而非一直搁着的程度
senses.example: The plan's solubility was doubted by every engineer on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会的每位工程师都怀疑这个方案有解。
senses.why: planning treats obstacles as soluble matter, so the noun measures how much of the obstacle can be absorbed.
senses.whyCN: 规划把障碍当作可溶之物，这个名词便衡量障碍能被吸收多少。

senses.title: The property of an equation being solvable
senses.definition: the property of an equation or logical problem that allows an answer to be found by rule
senses.definitionCN: 方程或逻辑问题能按规则求出答案的性质
senses.example: The solubility of the equation was proved in a single page.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程的可解性用一页纸就被证明了。
senses.why: mathematics borrowed the language of loosening for equations long before chemistry standardized the noun.
senses.whyCN: 数学早在化学规范这个名词之前，就借用了「松开」的说法来讲方程。

senses.title: How far a hard feeling can soften
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：难解心绪能被化解的程度
senses.definition: the degree to which grief, anger or resentment can be eased over time
senses.definitionCN: 悲伤、怒气或怨恨随时间能被缓解的程度
senses.example: The solubility of grief is not a matter of weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 悲伤能否化开，不是几周的事。
senses.why: the abstract use asks how much of a feeling a situation can absorb, which is the chemical image applied inward.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法追问一种处境能吸收多少情绪，正是化学意象转向内心。

intro.en: Solubility is soluble plus -ity 'state or quality', modelled on Late Latin solubilitas. The English word is recorded from the seventeenth century, when chemistry began measuring how much of a substance a solvent could take. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solubility 是 soluble 加 -ity「状态、性质」构成，仿晚期拉丁 solubilitas。英语自十七世纪有记录，正值化学开始测量溶剂能容纳多少物质。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere 'to loosen, untie, dissolve' joins se- 'apart' to luere 'to loosen'; its participle solutus gives the stem behind solution and solute.
items.cn: solvere「松开、解开、溶解」由 se-「分开」加 luere「松开」构成；其分词 solutus 提供 solution 与 solute 的词干。

items.en: Solubilis 'able to be dissolved' added -bilis to the same stem, and Late Latin formed the abstract noun solubilitas from it.
items.cn: solubilis「可被溶解的」在同一词干后加 -bilis，晚期拉丁由此构成抽象名词 solubilitas。

items.en: English built solubility on soluble with -ity in the seventeenth century, at first for the tendency of a body to dissolve.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪用 -ity 在 soluble 上构成 solubility，最初指物体溶解的倾向。

items.en: As chemists fixed temperature and weighed both solvent and solute, solubility came to name a measurable quantity as well as a quality.
items.cn: 当化学家固定温度并称量溶剂与溶质后，solubility 既指性质，也指可测量的数量。

items.en: The word has long been applied to problems and disputes, where it measures how far a difficulty can be loosened rather than how much solid a liquid can take.
items.cn: 这个词长期也被用于问题与争端，那里衡量的是困难能被松开多少，而非液体能容纳多少固体。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin form of luere is reconstructed, and the earliest English citation for the figurative sense is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：luere 在拉丁语之前的形式属于重构；比喻义最早英语书证没有确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the chemical family that is constantly swapped in speech; group two holds measured properties that look similar on a data sheet.
note.cn: 第一组是口语中常被互换的化学词族；第二组是在数据表上看起来相似的可测性质。

entries.definition: The adjective says that something can dissolve; the noun says how much or how readily it does so.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词说某物能溶解；名词说它溶多少、溶得多容易。

entries.definition: The solid or gas that is dissolved; it is the object measured, not the measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 被溶解的固体或气体，是被测量的对象，不是测量本身。

entries.definition: The liquid mixture that results from dissolving; a solution has a solubility, but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 溶解后得到的液体混合物；溶液有溶解度，但它本身不是溶解度。

entries.definition: An adjective for problems that can be solved; it looks close but has no chemical use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容可以解决的问题；形近，但无化学用法。

entries.definition: The ability of two liquids to mix, as water and ethanol; solubility is normally about a solid or gas in a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 两种液体相互混合的能力，如水与乙醇；solubility 通常指固体或气体溶于液体。

entries.definition: The amount of solute present in a given volume; solubility is the ceiling that concentration can reach.
entries.definitionCN: 给定体积中已含溶质的量；solubility 是浓度能达到的上限。

entries.definition: The ease with which a fluid passes through a solid; it concerns passage, not dissolving.
entries.definitionCN: 流体穿过固体的容易程度；说的是通过，不是溶解。

entries.definition: The thickness of a liquid; a syrup can have low solubility and high viscosity at the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 液体的黏稠程度；糖浆可以同时溶解度低而黏度高。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Soluble plus -ity: the ending turns the ability into a name.
normal.cn: soluble 加 -ity：这个结尾把能力变成名称。

normal.en: The family runs soluble, solubility, insoluble, insolubility, solute, solution.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 soluble、solubility、insoluble、insolubility、solute、solution。

normal.en: Data phrases mark the measured sense: high solubility, low solubility, solubility limit.
normal.cn: 数据说法标出测量义：高溶解度、低溶解度、溶解度极限。

normal.en: The solvent follows the noun: solubility in water, solubility in alcohol.
normal.cn: 名词后面跟着溶剂：在水中的溶解度、在酒精中的溶解度。

normal.en: Chemistry sets solubility against concentration, the ceiling against the current level.
normal.cn: 化学把溶解度与浓度对立：上限对当前水平。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer climbing while more and more sugar disappears.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计一路上升，越来越多的糖随之消失。

abstract.en: Picture a glass already full of dissolved sweet, refusing one more spoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯已经溶满甜味的液体，再多一勺也装不下。

abstract.en: Picture a hard quarrel that loosens a little each time the two sides meet.
abstract.cn: 想象一场僵持的争吵，每次双方见面就松开一点。

examples.en: The lab reports the solubility of each new compound before animal trials begin.
examples.cn: 实验室在动物试验开始前报告每种新化合物的溶解度。

examples.en: Low solubility in water makes the mineral hard to leach from soil.
examples.cn: 在水中的低溶解度使这种矿物难以从土壤中淋出。

examples.en: The mediator spoke about the solubility of the conflict, not its causes.
examples.cn: 调解人谈的是这场冲突能否化解，而不是它的起因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「solu（松开）+ bility（能）」——能松开的程度：溶解度、可解决性

root: 拉丁 solubilitas「可溶性」= solubilis（可被溶解的）+ -itas（性质）；solubilis 出自 solvere（松开、解开），由 se-（分开）+ luere（松开）构成。英语以 soluble + -ity 构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses measure one loosening: how readily a solid dissolves, how much of it a solvent takes, which solvent is named, how a drug behaves in the body, how far a problem, a plan, an equation and finally a hard feeling can be loosened.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在衡量同一次松开：固体多容易溶解，溶剂能容纳多少，被点名的是哪种溶剂，药物在体内如何表现，以及一个问题、一个方案、一个方程，最后一种难解心绪能被松开多少。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale beside a glass, showing how much of a solid the liquid has taken.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子旁边放着一把量尺，显示液体已经容纳了多少固体。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND NUMBER: the same quality is read first as an ability and then as a measured amount.
branches.cn: 能力与数量：同一性质先被读作能力，再被读作可测的数量。

branches.en: SPECIFIC LIQUIDS: naming the solvent and naming the body fluid both tie the measure to a particular medium.
branches.cn: 特定液体：点名溶剂与点名体液，都把量度系在特定介质上。

branches.en: PROBLEMS AND PLANS: difficulties and proposals are weighed by how much of them can be absorbed.
branches.cn: 问题与方案：困难与提议都按「能被吸收多少」来称量。

branches.en: EQUATIONS: mathematics measures loosening by whether a rule can find the answer.
branches.cn: 方程：数学以规则能否求出答案来衡量松开的程度。

branches.en: FEELINGS: grief is tested for how much a situation can dissolve.
branches.cn: 情绪：悲伤被检验的是处境能化开多少。

intro.en: Solubility is a Latin-derived adjective plus a Latin suffix, and the pieces still build the whole chemical family.
intro.cn: solubility 是一个拉丁来源的形容词加上一个拉丁后缀，各部分仍在构成整个化学词族。

latinIntro.en: -itas becomes -ity in English and names a state or quality; solvere 'to loosen' stands behind soluble, solution, solute and dissolve.
latinIntro.cn: -itas 在英语中变为 -ity，表示状态或性质；solvere「松开」是 soluble、solution、solute 与 dissolve 的共同来源。

items.meaningCN: 处于某种状态、具有某种性质
items.example: The suffix turns soluble into the name of a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 soluble 变成一种性质的名称。
它在 solvere 上构成 solubilis。

items.example: The root is the image inside the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是整个词族里的那幅画面。

items.example: The verb is the source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的源头。

items.example: The salt is soluble in warm water.
Solubility falls as the water cools.
items.exampleCN: 水温下降时溶解度降低。

items.example: Insolubility kept the powder out of the mixture.
items.exampleCN: 不可溶性使这种粉末无法进入混合物。

items.example: The solute was weighed to the nearest milligram.
The solution turned clear after heating.

items.meaning: to come apart in a liquid
items.example: The crystals dissolve slowly in cold water.
items.exampleCN: 晶体在冷水中缓慢溶解。

definition_zh: 可溶的；能溶解的；（难题、谜团）可解决的
definition_en: able to be dissolved in a liquid, or able to be solved or explained
core_image: 一块方糖沉进温水，棱角一圈圈化开，最后杯底只剩一点甜
scene: 实验台上，学生把一小块白色晶体放进温水，晶体很快散开，杯底不留残渣。The white crystal proved highly soluble in warm water.
sceneCN: 这里 soluble 指物质能在液体里被溶解（第 1 个义项：能在液体中溶散）；句意为这块白色晶体在温水中极易溶解。图中可辨识物件：烧杯、温水、玻璃棒、晶体。

pos.zh: （问题、谜团）可解决的；可解释的

senses.title: Able to dissolve in a liquid
senses.definition: capable of being dissolved in a liquid and mixed into it so completely that no solid remains visible
senses.definitionCN: 能在液体中溶解并完全混入其中，看不出固体残留
senses.example: Sugar is soluble in warm water.
senses.exampleCN: 糖能溶于温水。
senses.why: soluble descends from Latin solvere 'to loosen', so the core picture is a solid whose particles are loosened apart by a liquid.
senses.whyCN: soluble 出自拉丁 solvere「松开」，核心画面是固体的微粒被液体拆散。

senses.title: Dissolving in a named solvent
senses.titleCN: 对某种指定溶剂的溶解性
senses.definition: dissolving in the particular liquid that is named, rather than dissolving in any liquid at all
senses.definitionCN: 能溶于被点名的那种液体，而不是泛指任何液体
senses.example: This resin is soluble in alcohol but not in water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种树脂溶于酒精，却不溶于水。
senses.why: dissolving is always a relation between two things, so naming the solvent turns a bare ability into a measured pair.
senses.whyCN: 溶解总是两样东西之间的关系，点明溶剂就把笼统的能力变成一对具体的搭配。

senses.title: A problem that can be solved
senses.definition: able to be settled or worked out, said of a difficulty rather than of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 指困难可以被处理、被解决，而非指物质
senses.example: The dispute proved soluble once both sides met.
senses.exampleCN: 双方一见面，这场纠纷便显出可以化解。
senses.why: the Latin root also meant 'to untie a knot', and a difficulty that can be untied is one that can be solved.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根还表示「解开绳结」，能解开的困难就是能解决的问题。

senses.title: A puzzle that can be explained
senses.definition: capable of being explained or answered, said of a riddle, a question or a mystery
senses.definitionCN: 指谜语、疑问或谜团能够被解释、被回答
senses.example: The riddle was soluble with a single clue.
senses.exampleCN: 只要一条线索，这个谜语就能解开。
senses.why: a riddle is a knot tied in thought, so loosening it is the same gesture as solving it.
senses.whyCN: 谜语是打在思路上的结，把它松开与把它解出是同一个动作。

senses.title: A difference that can be reconciled
senses.definition: able to be brought into agreement, said of views, claims or interests that are opposed
senses.definitionCN: 指对立的看法、主张或利益能够被调和一致
senses.example: Their differences were soluble through a neutral arbiter.
senses.exampleCN: 经一位中立的仲裁者，他们的分歧得以调和。
senses.why: two positions tied against each other can be untied, and that untieing is what dissolving means at root.
senses.whyCN: 两个相互抵住的立场可以解开，而「解开」正是 dissolve 与 soluble 的本义。

senses.title: Able to be loosened, an old use
senses.definition: able to be undone or loosened, said of a knot, a band or a fastening in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中指绳结、束带或系缚能够被解开
senses.example: An old text might call a knot that can be undone soluble.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文献可能把能解开的结称作 soluble。
senses.why: this is the oldest physical sense, and chemistry later kept only the image of parts coming apart.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的实体义，化学后来只保留了「各部分散开」这一层。

senses.title: A fertiliser that dissolves in irrigation water
senses.titleCN: 可随灌溉水施用的可溶性肥料
senses.definition: able to be dissolved in water so that it can be delivered through an irrigation system
senses.definitionCN: 能溶于水，从而可经灌溉系统施入田间
senses.example: Farmers spread soluble fertiliser through the irrigation line.
senses.exampleCN: 农民通过灌溉管道施用可溶性肥料。
senses.why: the technical sense narrows the first one: a fertiliser that dissolves in water can travel with the water.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义是把第一义收窄：能溶于水的肥料可以跟着水走。

senses.title: A feeling that might soften
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：情绪或心结可以化解
senses.definition: able to be eased or softened, said figuratively of grief, anger or a hard feeling
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指悲伤、怒气或难解的心绪能够被缓解、被冲淡
senses.example: Her grief was not soluble in a single conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 一次谈话化不开她的悲伤。
senses.why: the abstract use treats a feeling as a substance that may or may not dissolve, which is the root image carried into the mind.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法把情绪当成可能溶、也可能不溶的物质，正是词根意象被带入心里。

intro.en: Soluble comes through Old French from Late Latin solubilis 'that may be dissolved', built on solvere 'to loosen, untie, dissolve' plus -bilis 'able to'. It is recorded in English from the fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: soluble 经古法语来自晚期拉丁 solubilis「可被溶解的」，由 solvere「松开、解开、溶解」加 -bilis「能够」构成，十四世纪起在英语中有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, release, dissolve'. It is built from se- 'apart' plus luere 'to loosen', and the same verb also gives solve, solution and dissolve.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、释放、溶解」，由 se-「分开」加 luere「松开」构成，同一动词也衍生出 solve、solution 与 dissolve。

items.en: The past participle solutus 'loosened, dissolved' supplied the stem solut-, which appears in solution, solute and absolutus 'set free'.
items.cn: 过去分词 solutus「松开的、溶解的」提供了 solut- 词干，出现在 solution、solute 与 absolutus「释放」中。

items.en: Late Latin solubilis added -bilis 'able to be' to the same stem, giving a word that could describe a substance as dissolvable.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 solubilis 在同一词干后加 -bilis「能够被……」，用来形容某物质可被溶解。

items.en: Old French soluble passed into English in the fourteenth century, first for substances that melt or break up in water.
items.cn: 古法语 soluble 在十四世纪进入英语，最初用于在水中熔化或散开的物质。

items.en: From the seventeenth century chemists fixed the word to the relation between a substance and a named solvent, which produced stable phrases such as soluble in water and soluble in alcohol.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，化学家把这个词固定为物质与指定溶剂之间的关系，于是出现「溶于水」「溶于酒精」这类稳定说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of luere is reconstructed as a root meaning 'to loosen', and the exact first English citation is not recorded; the reconstruction is offered as a form, not as a demonstrated word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：luere 在拉丁语之前的形态被重构为一个表示「松开」的词根，英语最早书证的确切年代没有记录；该形式是重构形式，并非已证实的词。

note.en: Group one holds words from the solvere stock, where prefixes change what is being loosened; group two holds words that sound like they measure dissolving but do not.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 solvere 词干的词，前缀改变「被松开」的对象；第二组是听起来像在描述溶解、实际并非如此的词。

entries.definition: The bare verb 'to loosen': to find the answer to a problem, with no chemical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的「松开」动词：找出问题的答案，不含化学义。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus solvere: the act by which a solid comes apart in a liquid; it names an event, while soluble names a capacity.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 solvere：固体在液体中散开的过程，指事件；soluble 则指能力。

entries.definition: The mixture produced by dissolving, or the answer produced by solving; the noun sits after the action.
entries.definitionCN: 溶解后得到的混合物，或解题得到的答案；名词位于动作之后。

entries.definition: Ab- 'away' plus solvere: loosened from every limit, hence complete and unrestricted; it shares the root but not the sense.
entries.definitionCN: ab-「离开」加 solvere：从一切限制中松开，故指完全、无条件；词根相同而词义不同。

entries.definition: Used of liquids that mix into each other, as water and alcohol; it does not describe a solid entering a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 用于彼此混合的液体，如水与酒精；不描述固体进入液体。

entries.definition: Able to be dissolved, closer to the action of dissolving than to a measured chemical property.
entries.definitionCN: 能被溶解，偏向溶解动作，而非可测量的化学性质。

entries.definition: Able to be solved; it never carries the chemical sense that soluble carries.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被解决；从不带 soluble 那样的化学义。

entries.definition: Describes a material that a fluid can pass through, not a substance that enters a liquid and becomes part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述流体可以穿过的材料，而非进入液体并成为其一部分的物质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Solvere 'to loosen': the solid is loosened apart inside the liquid.
normal.cn: solvere「松开」：固体在液体内部被拆散。

normal.en: The family runs solve, dissolve, solution, solute and solubility.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 solve、dissolve、solution、solute 与 solubility。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the solvent: soluble in water, soluble in alcohol.
normal.cn: 固定搭配会点明溶剂：溶于水、溶于酒精。

normal.en: The opposite is insoluble, built with the negative prefix in-.
normal.cn: 反义词是 insoluble，用否定前缀 in- 构成。

normal.en: Chemistry pairs the word with the two everyday solids, salt and sugar.
normal.cn: 化学常把这个词与盐、糖这两种日常固体配在一起。

root: 拉丁 solubilis「可被溶解的」= solvere（松开、解开、溶解）+ -bilis（能够）；solvere 由 se-（分开）+ luere（松开）构成，luere 的更早形态为重构形式。英语经古法语 soluble 进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one loosening: a solid is loosened in a liquid, the solvent is named, a knot is untied, a problem and a riddle are untied in the mind, a quarrel is loosened, a fertiliser is dissolved into irrigation water, and a feeling is finally tested for whether it can dissolve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「松开」：固体在液体里被拆散，溶剂被点名，绳结被解开，问题与谜语在脑中解开，争吵被化开，肥料溶进灌溉水，最后是一种情绪被检验能否化解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid losing its edges inside a liquid until nothing visible is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块固体在液体里失去棱角，直到看不见残留。

branches.en: DISSOLVING: the bare capacity and the solvent-specific relation are two readings of the same test.
branches.cn: 溶解：笼统的能力与指明溶剂的关系，是同一次检验的两种读法。

branches.en: UNTIED IN THE MIND: a difficulty and a riddle are knots that come loose.
branches.cn: 在脑中解开：困难与谜语都是可以松开的结。

branches.en: LOOSENED BONDS: opposed claims and a physical knot share the oldest image.
branches.cn: 松开的束缚：对立的主张与实在的绳结共享最古老的意象。

branches.en: DISSOLVED INTO WATER: the farm sense narrows dissolving to a fertiliser carried by irrigation.
branches.cn: 溶进水：农业义把溶解收窄为随灌溉水走的肥料。

branches.en: SOFTENED FEELING: grief and anger are treated as substances that may or may not dissolve.
branches.cn: 软化的情绪：悲伤与怒气被当作可能溶、也可能不溶的物质。

intro.en: Soluble is a Latin adjective built from a prefix, a verb root and a suffix, and every piece also builds other English words.
intro.cn: soluble 是一个拉丁形容词，由前缀、动词词根与后缀构成，每一部分也都参与构成其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere gives solve, dissolve, solution and absolute; -bilis marks what can be done, and it survives as -able and -ible in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solvere 衍生 solve、dissolve、solution 与 absolute；-bilis 表示「能够被……」，在英语中留下 -able 与 -ible。

senses.title: Financially able to pay debts

senses.exampleCN: 在多数生物反应中，水是溶剂。

senses.whyCN: 混合物中必须有一个组分执行溶解，通常就是占得更多、更易移动的那一部分。

senses.title: Having the power to dissolve

senses.example: The workshop banned the old solvent after the ventilation report.
senses.exampleCN: 通风报告之后，车间禁用了那种旧溶剂。
senses.why: grease and resin will not wash away in water, so workshops need a stronger liquid to carry them off.
senses.whyCN: 油脂与树脂不能靠水洗掉，车间因此需要更强的液体把它们带走。

senses.title: Solvent abuse as inhalants
senses.titleCN: 作为吸入剂的溶剂滥用
senses.definition: the practice of inhaling fumes from glues and cleaners for a short-lived high
senses.definitionCN: 为获得短暂快感而吸入胶水或清洁剂蒸气的行为
senses.example: Solvent abuse among teenagers worried the school.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年吸食溶剂让学校担忧。
senses.why: the same volatile fumes that dissolve grease can be inhaled, which is why the word appears in warnings.
senses.whyCN: 溶开油脂的同一挥发性蒸气也能被吸入，因此这个词出现在警示语中。

senses.title: A solvent estate in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上足以清偿的遗产
senses.definition: an estate whose assets are enough to pay the deceased person's debts and gifts
senses.definitionCN: 资产足以支付死者债务与遗赠的遗产
senses.example: The executor confirmed that the estate was solvent.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱执行人确认这笔遗产足以清偿。
senses.why: the test for an estate is the same as for a firm: do the assets cover what must be paid out?
senses.whyCN: 对遗产的检验与对企业相同：资产是否覆盖必须付出的款项？

senses.title: Solvent extraction as a process
senses.definition: a method that uses a liquid to pull a wanted substance out of a solid or another liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用液体把目标物质从固体或另一液体中提取出来的方法
senses.example: Oil is often recovered by solvent extraction from crushed seed.
senses.exampleCN: 油常通过溶剂萃取从压碎的种子中提取。
senses.why: a liquid can carry a wanted substance out of a solid, which turns the chemical property into an industrial method.
senses.whyCN: 液体能把目标物质从固体中带出，这一化学性质于是变成工业方法。

senses.title: Solvent-free products
senses.definition: describing paints, glues or cleaners made without volatile organic liquids
senses.definitionCN: 描述不使用挥发性有机液体的油漆、胶水或清洁剂
senses.example: The builder switched to solvent-free adhesives for indoor work.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方在室内作业改用无溶剂胶黏剂。
senses.why: if the fumes are the problem, the simplest fix is to make the product without any solvent at all.
senses.whyCN: 如果问题出在蒸气，最简单的办法就是完全不用溶剂来制造产品。

intro.en: Solvent is the present participle of Latin solvere 'to loosen, pay'. English uses it for both paying and dissolving because the Latin verb covers both. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solvent 是拉丁 solvere「松开、清偿」的现在分词。英语用它兼指偿付与溶解，因为拉丁动词本来就覆盖两义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve, pay'. The two modern senses of solvent were both present in the Latin verb, one as untying a debt and one as loosening a substance.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解、清偿」。solvent 的两个现代义在拉丁动词中都已存在，一是解开债务，一是溶开物质。

items.en: The present participle solvens meant 'loosening, paying', and English took the form directly rather than through a noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 solvens 意为「正在松开、正在清偿」，英语直接吸收这一形式，而非经由名词。

items.en: Alchemists and later chemists used solvent for the liquid that dissolves a solid, a sense recorded in English from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 炼金术士与后来的化学家用 solvent 指溶解固体的液体，这一义自 17 世纪见于英语。

items.en: The financial sense, able to pay what one owes, is also recorded in the seventeenth century and rests on the paying half of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 「能够清偿所欠」的财务义同样见于 17 世纪，依据的是拉丁动词中「清偿」的那一半。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries made solvents ordinary industrial materials, and the word spread to cleaning, painting and extraction.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪使溶剂成为寻常工业材料，这个词扩展到清洁、涂装与萃取。

items.en: Late in the twentieth century, concern about fumes produced the compound solvent-free and a new sense of the word.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期对蒸气的担忧产生了「无溶剂」这一复合词与该词的新义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the loosening root or the same chemical field; group two holds financial adjectives that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「松开」词根或同属化学领域的词；第二组是常与它混淆的财务形容词。

entries.definition: The substance that is dissolved; the solvent is what does the dissolving, so the two are opposites in a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 指被溶解的物质；溶剂是执行溶解的一方，二者在混合物中相对。

entries.definition: The resulting mixture of solute and solvent, or an answer to a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 指溶质与溶剂形成的混合物，或问题的解答。

entries.definition: Describing the solute that can go into a solvent; it does not describe the liquid itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能进入溶剂的溶质；并不描述液体本身。

entries.definition: The ability to pay debts; the adjective for that ability is solvent.
entries.definitionCN: 指偿债能力；表示该能力的形容词正是 solvent。

entries.definition: Judged safe to lend to; a firm can be solvent yet judged uncreditworthy.
entries.definitionCN: 指被认为可以安全放贷；企业可以有偿付能力却仍被认为不宜放贷。

entries.definition: Able to turn assets into cash quickly; solvency concerns totals, not speed.
entries.definitionCN: 指能迅速把资产变成现金；偿付能力关乎总额，而非速度。

entries.definition: A dissolving agent, used in technical writing; solvent is the common form.
entries.definitionCN: 指起溶解作用之物，用于技术写作；solvent 是常见形式。

entries.definition: Describing an amount that must be paid; solvent describes the one who can pay it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述应支付的款项；solvent 描述有能力支付的人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One Latin verb, two jobs: untie a debt and loosen a solid, so solvent means both able to pay and able to dissolve.
normal.cn: 一个拉丁动词干两件事：解开债务与溶开固体，所以这个词既指能清偿，也指能溶解。

normal.en: The family runs solve, solution, soluble, solvent, solvency, insolvent, dissolve.
normal.cn: 同族词包括解决、溶液、可溶的、溶剂、偿付能力、无力偿付的、溶解。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: organic solvent, solvent extraction, solvent abuse, remain solvent.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出用法：有机溶剂、溶剂萃取、吸食溶剂、保持偿付能力。

normal.en: In a mixture the solvent is the liquid, the solute is what disappears into it.
normal.cn: 在混合物中，溶剂是液体，溶质是溶进其中的东西。

normal.en: Solvent-free paint is a modern label made by putting the old word in front of free.
normal.cn: 无溶剂油漆是把旧词放在「无」前面造出的现代标签。

abstract.en: Picture a clear liquid eating a sugar lump while a settled bill hangs on the bottle.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶透明液体正在化开糖块，瓶上挂着已结清的账单。

abstract.en: Picture a knot coming undone with no knife, only patience.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绳结在没有刀的情况下慢慢解开，只靠耐心。

abstract.en: Picture two faces of one coin: one reads able to pay, the other reads able to dissolve.
abstract.cn: 想象同一枚硬币的两面：一面写「能清偿」，一面写「能溶解」。

examples.en: The firm remained solvent even after the loss, because its property was worth more than its debt.
examples.cn: 即使出现亏损，这家企业仍有偿付能力，因为其房产价值高于债务。

examples.en: Use the solvent outdoors; the fumes are heavier than air.
examples.cn: 要在户外使用这种溶剂，其蒸气比空气重。

examples.en: The estate was solvent, so every creditor was paid in full.
examples.cn: 这笔遗产足以清偿，因此每位债权人都获得全额支付。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses use one participle in two fields: a payer who can untie debts, and a liquid that unties solids, then the cleaning trade, inhalant misuse, estates, extraction and products made without it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个分词用在两个领域：能解开债务的清偿者，能溶开固体的液体，随后是清洁行业、吸入滥用、遗产、萃取，以及不含它的产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear liquid eating a sugar lump, with a settled bill hanging on the bottle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一瓶透明液体正在化开糖块，瓶上挂着已结清的账单。

branches.en: THE PAYER: a person, a firm or an estate that can untie what it owes.
branches.cn: 清偿者：能解开所欠之债的个人、企业或遗产。

branches.en: THE LIQUID AND ITS POWER: the dissolving component, and the strength it brings.
branches.cn: 液体与力量：执行溶解的组分，以及它所带的溶解力。

branches.en: THE TRADE: cleaning fluids and extraction methods turn the chemical sense into work.
branches.cn: 行业：清洁液与萃取方法把化学义变成工作。

branches.en: MISUSE: the same fumes that clean metal can be inhaled.
branches.cn: 滥用：清洁金属的同一蒸气也可被吸入。

branches.en: THE NEGATIVE FORM: modern products are labelled by the absence of the solvent.
branches.cn: 否定形式：现代产品以「不含溶剂」来标注。

senses.example: A strange sound came from the distance.

senses.title: To seem when heard
senses.definition: to give a certain impression when heard
senses.definitionCN: 被听见时给人某种印象
senses.example: That plan sounds good to me.

definition_zh: 君主；主权国家；英国旧时一镑金币；握有最高权力的；独立自主的；（药）极有效的；完全的
definition_en: a supreme ruler or an independent state; as an adjective, holding supreme power, self-governing, highly effective or complete
core_image: 一枚金币正面铸着君主侧面像，边缘的齿纹像国界的界桩
scene: 展柜里躺着一枚旧金币，正面是君主侧面像，旁边放着一份独立国家的条约副本。The sovereign refused to let a foreign court review the decree.
sceneCN: 这里 sovereign 指「握有最高权力、不受外部复审的君主或国家」（第 1 个义项：君主本人）；句意为这位君主拒绝让外国法庭复审这项敕令。可辨识物件：展柜、金币、侧面像、条约副本、敕令。

pos.zh: 君主；主权国家；英国旧时一镑金币
握有最高权力的；独立自主的；极有效的；完全的

derivatives.zh: sovereign + -ty（状态后缀，源自拉丁 -tas）→ 主权，语义由握权者转为抽象权力
sovereign + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以最高权力方式地
古法语 suserain（不带插入的 g）→ 宗主，语义由完全主权降为部分主权
sovereignty + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 主权主义者，主张把权力留在本国

senses.title: A supreme ruler
senses.definition: a king, queen or other ruler who holds supreme authority
senses.definitionCN: 握有最高权威的国王、女王或其他统治者
senses.example: The sovereign refused to let a foreign court review the decree.
senses.exampleCN: 这位君主拒绝让外国法庭复审这项敕令。
senses.why: The adjective 'above all others' became a noun for the person who occupies that top place.
senses.whyCN: 形容词「居于一切之上」转为名词，指占据那个最高位置的人。

senses.title: A former British gold coin
senses.definition: a British gold coin worth one pound sterling, minted until the early twentieth century
senses.definitionCN: 英国旧时面值一英镑的金币，铸造至二十世纪初
senses.example: A sovereign hung on a chain in the museum case.
senses.exampleCN: 展柜里，一枚金币挂在链子上。
senses.why: Coins were named after the portrait of the sovereign stamped on them, so the ruler's title became the coin's name.
senses.whyCN: 硬币以铸在其上的君主肖像命名，于是统治者的称号成了硬币之名。

senses.title: Holding supreme power
senses.definition: possessing final authority that no other body can override
senses.definitionCN: 拥有任何其他机构都无法推翻的最终权威
senses.example: The sovereign assembly could repeal any law.
senses.exampleCN: 这个最高议会可以废除任何法律。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the original spatial image: the sovereign body sits above every other body.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词保留了原初的空间意象：主权机构位于所有其他机构之上。

senses.title: Independent and self-governing
senses.definition: describing a state that governs itself and is not subject to another's laws
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个自我治理、不受他国法律约束的国家
senses.example: A sovereign state cannot be bound by another country's courts.
senses.exampleCN: 主权国家不受他国法庭约束。
senses.why: If no power is above a state, then it is above every other state's jurisdiction, which is independence.
senses.whyCN: 如果没有权力高于一国，那么它也不受任何他国管辖，这便是独立。

senses.title: Extremely effective as a remedy
senses.definition: having a sure and powerful effect in curing a problem, used especially of medicines
senses.definitionCN: 在解决问题上确有强效，尤用于药物
senses.example: Honey was once a sovereign remedy for wounds.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂蜜曾是治疗伤口的特效药。
senses.why: A remedy that works above all others takes the same adjective of supremacy, so sovereign came to mean 'sure'.
senses.whyCN: 效力高于一切其他手段的药方也取用这个「最高」形容词，于是 sovereign 有了「确效」之义。

senses.title: Of the highest worth
senses.definition: ranking first among goods or aims, as in philosophical discussion of the highest good
senses.definitionCN: 在诸善或诸目标中居于首位，如哲学讨论中的最高善
senses.example: Scholars debated the sovereign good of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们辩论城邦的最高善。
senses.why: The word's rank sense fits moral philosophy, where one good is above all the others.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的等级义适合道德哲学，其中有一种善高于其余一切。

senses.title: Complete and unlimited
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean total, as in sovereign contempt or sovereign right
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前表示彻底，如完全的蔑视或绝对的权利
senses.example: He treated the proposal with sovereign contempt.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这项提议报以彻底的蔑视。
senses.why: An attitude held by a ruler needs no one's approval, so 'sovereign' before a noun marks a feeling that admits no limit.
senses.whyCN: 统治者的态度无需任何人批准，因此名词前的 sovereign 标记一种不受限制的情绪。

senses.title: Of a state's official debt or immunity
senses.titleCN: 国家主权债务或豁免的
senses.definition: relating to a state in its capacity as a borrower or as a legal person immune from suit
senses.definitionCN: 指国家作为借款人或免于被诉的法律人格
senses.example: Sovereign debt worries markets more than corporate borrowing.
senses.exampleCN: 主权债务比企业借贷更令市场担忧。
senses.why: Finance needed a word for the state's own borrowing, and the state's supreme legal standing supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 金融需要一个词指国家自身的借贷，而国家的最高法律地位提供了这个词。

intro.en: Sovereign comes through Old French soverain from Vulgar Latin superanus 'chief', from Latin super 'above'. The g in English spelling has no settled explanation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sovereign 经古法语 soverain 来自通俗拉丁 superanus「首领」，再上溯拉丁 super「在上」。英语拼写中的 g 没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Super 'above, over' is the root of rank words such as superior and supervise.
items.cn: super「在上、超过」是 superior、supervise 等表示等级的词的词根。

items.en: Superanus meant 'chief, the one above', formed with the adjective suffix -anus.
items.cn: superanus 意为「首领、居上者」，由形容词后缀 -anus 构成。

items.en: Old French soverain carried the word to English, where the spelling gained a g that no Latin or French form shows.
items.cn: 古法语 soverain 把词带入英语，英语拼写多出一个 g，而拉丁或法语形式都没有这个字母。

items.en: From 1817 the gold pound coin was called a sovereign because it bore the monarch's portrait.
items.cn: 自 1817 年起，一英镑金币因铸有君主肖像而被称为 sovereign。

items.en: International law and finance extended the adjective to states, producing sovereign immunity and sovereign debt.
items.cn: 国际法与金融把这个形容词扩展到国家，产生主权豁免与主权债务。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the intrusive g has never been fully explained, and the earliest English citation is not established; forms without it survive in suzerain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：插入的 g 从未得到完满解释，最早的英语书证也未确定；不带 g 的形式保存在 suzerain 中。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same superanus stock or accidental look-alikes; group two holds words for supreme or independent power.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 superanus 词干或偶然形近的形式；第二组是表示最高或独立权力的词。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the authority itself; sovereign is the holder or the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指权威本身的抽象名词；sovereign 指握有者或形容词。

entries.definition: The same Old French base without the inserted g: a lord over a state that keeps internal self-rule.
entries.definitionCN: 同一古法语词基而不带插入的 g：凌驾于一国之上、却让其内部自治的宗主。

entries.definition: Latin comparative of super, 'higher'; it shares the root but means relative rank, not supreme legal power.
entries.definitionCN: super 的拉丁比较级「更高的」；共享词根，但指相对等级，而非最高法律权力。

entries.definition: From superbus 'proud, splendid': excellent. The spelling suggests kinship, but the sense developed separately.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 superbus「骄傲、辉煌」：极佳的。拼写显得同族，但语义另有发展。

entries.definition: A sole hereditary ruler; sovereign may be any supreme authority, including an elected assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 唯一的世袭统治者；sovereign 可指任何最高权威，包括经选举的议会。

entries.definition: Free from outside control; it stresses the fact of freedom, while sovereign stresses legal supremacy.
entries.definitionCN: 不受外部控制；强调自由的事实，而 sovereign 强调法律上的最高性。

entries.definition: Highest in rank or degree; it is a plainer adjective and lacks the political and legal history of sovereign.
entries.definitionCN: 等级或程度上最高的；是更朴素的形容词，没有 sovereign 那样的政治与法律史。

entries.definition: More important than all others; it ranks concerns, not institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 比其余一切更重要；排列的是事务，而非机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: super 'above' + -anus 'belonging to': the one belonging above all others.
normal.cn: super「在上」+ -anus「属于」：属于所有人之上的那一个。

normal.en: The family runs sovereign, sovereignty, sovereignly, suzerain, suzerainty.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sovereign、sovereignty、sovereignly、suzerain、suzerainty。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sovereign state, sovereign debt, sovereign immunity, sovereign remedy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：主权国家、主权债务、主权豁免、特效药。

normal.en: The gold coin was named after the portrait on its face.
normal.cn: 金币因币面上的肖像而得名。

normal.en: suzerain preserves the older spelling without the unexplained g.
normal.cn: suzerain 保留了不带那个无法解释的 g 的较早拼写。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose face is a ruler and whose edge is a border.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚金币，正面是君主，边缘是国界。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom with a sign saying no appeal beyond this room.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，挂着「此室外无上诉」的牌子。

abstract.en: Picture a medicine that works before the diagnosis is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象一种药，诊断还没结束就已见效。

examples.en: Each sovereign state prints its own passports.
examples.cn: 每个主权国家都印自己的护照。

examples.en: The coin dealer offered him a sovereign from the old mint.
examples.cn: 钱币商向他出售一枚旧铸币厂的金币。

examples.en: Investors watched sovereign debt as closely as company earnings.
examples.cn: 投资者关注主权债务，如同关注公司盈利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sovereign」音近「谁负人」——没人能负在他之上，因为他是最高统治者 → 君主、主权的

root: 古法语 soverain「首领」← 通俗拉丁 superanus「居上者」← 拉丁 super「在上」+ -anus（形容词后缀）。英语 sovereign，插入的 g 来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one position at the top: a person, a coin, an assembly, a state, a medicine, a good, a mood and a debt can all be described as beyond appeal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「居于顶端」的位置展开：人、硬币、议会、国家、药物、善、情绪与债务都可以被称为「无从上诉」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gold coin bearing a ruler's profile, its milled edge like a row of border stones.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚铸着君主侧面像的金币，齿边像一排界桩。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one who occupies the top place in a realm.
branches.cn: 人：在疆域中占据最高位置的那一个。

branches.en: THE COIN: a portrait turns a title into a piece of money.
branches.cn: 硬币：一张肖像把称号变成一枚钱币。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: an assembly or a state acts beyond any appeal.
branches.cn: 机构：议会或国家行事不受任何上诉约束。

branches.en: THE STATE: no foreign court sits above it.
branches.cn: 国家：没有外国法庭位于其上。

branches.en: ABSOLUTE QUALITY: a cure, a good or a contempt that admits no rival.
branches.cn: 绝对性质：一种疗法、一种善或一种蔑视，都不容对手。

intro.en: Sovereign is a Latin-rooted adjective that became a noun, and its parts recur in English, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: sovereign 是由拉丁词根构成的形容词，后转为名词，其成分在英语中反复出现，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin super and superanus give sovereign and suzerain; the abstract ending -ty gives sovereignty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 super 与 superanus 衍生 sovereign 与 suzerain；抽象词尾 -ty 衍生 sovereignty。

items.exampleCN: superanus 指居于其余之上者。
这个国家捍卫自己的主权。
